semantic_boundary: This ledger enumerates accepted WP1 obligations and the exact fifteenth-review closure only. It creates no product semantics, does not accept WP1, and does not authorize WP2, WP3 execution, credentials, helper execution, network, or provider work.

identity_procedure.bytes: exact tracked UTF-8 file bytes, including the final LF
identity_procedure.binding: The append-only Slice 6 record stores this file's byte count and SHA-256. The convergence review must name both values, this ledger_id, and implementation_candidate_commit. Any byte change creates a different ledger and requires owner authorization before widening the checkpoint.

scope_classification.wp1_must_fix: Only an exact accepted WP1 requirement with a concrete reproducible schema, codec, persistence, compatibility, migration, output, replay, or traceability counterexample.
scope_classification.wp2: Coordinator reservation and final-gate behavior, simulator execution, operational settlement services, concurrency, and fault recovery. WP1 owns only their representable contract shapes.
scope_classification.wp3: Helper process execution and credential lifecycle implementation. WP1 owns only their closed contracts and protocol identities.
scope_classification.follow_up_or_non_blocking: Optional hardening, hypothetical future behavior, and properties not required by accepted authority cannot block WP1.
scope_classification.owner_decision: A missing or conflicting accepted semantic decision, or the accepted conservative-input-bound escalation, pauses only the affected path.
scope_classification.review_finiteness: A convergence-review must-fix must cite accepted WP1 authority, provide a reproducible counterexample, name one ledger item, and explain why the finding is not WP2, WP3, optional hardening, or an owner decision.

acceptance_items.title: Nine closed product schemas
acceptance_items.required: All nine schemas are closed, bounded, strict, versioned, canonical, and represent the explicit unavailable and terminal state vocabulary without secrets or expected answers.

Slice 6 plan section 7, schema 6 tables and compatibility declarations

acceptance_items.title: Evidence-acquisition ownership
acceptance_items.required: Evidence-acquisition runs are immutable operation owners with exact parent, detachment, application, provider/account, usage, cost, and replay links; analysis-run and acquisition-run ownership are not collapsed.

acceptance_items.title: Effective scan configuration v2 and additive provider publication

acceptance_items.required: Every provider-active operation uses effective-scan-configuration/v2 with the exact stateless/cache-off profile and finite limits. Provider publication is an additive supplement and v2 output/summary expose only non-secret operation, acquisition, admission, usage/cost/hold, replay, drift, and gap references.

acceptance_items.title: Slice 5 v1 byte and semantic compatibility
acceptance_items.required: The existing local-only effective-scan-configuration/v1 and publication overload remain byte-for-byte compatible and retain their exact provider-not-used semantics. No v1 dual interpretation, compatibility wrapper, or Slice 5 truth change is allowed.

acceptance_items.title: Helper v2 additive identity without v1 reinterpretation
authority: Slice 6 plan section 7, helper-private protocol v2
acceptance_items.required: Helper v2 has a new exact protocol identity and transitive fingerprint. Helper v1 retains the accepted bytes, descriptor field names and numbers, enum wire meanings, and independent decoding semantics. Privileged unknowns fail closed.

acceptance_items.title: Strict round trips and invalid-state totality
authority: Slice 6 plan section 12, Vertical deliverables and Retained evidence
acceptance_items.required: Every representable contract state has strict domain, JSON, protobuf, persistence, output, and replay behavior. Cross-state identities, quantities, projections, omissions, nulls, unknowns, and invalid states reject or degrade exactly as declared before the current proof-maturity gate.

acceptance_items.title: Conservative local input-bound proof or exact escalation
authority: Slice 6 plan section 12, Vertical deliverables and Escalation
acceptance_items.required: Admission proves the local input-token ceiling from exact canonical UTF-8 request bytes using an accepted exact local tokenizer or a separately qualified conservative provider-framing/structural-margin policy. Provider input-token-count is not a WP1 admission call; failure to prove the bound blocks WP1 rather than silently raising a ceiling.

accepted_escalation.condition: The repository has no accepted repository-local tokenizer or provider-framing proof from which the conservative bound can be established without an additional provider operation.
accepted_escalation.smallest_owner_decision: Accept or supply one exact repository-local tokenizer/provider-framing proof or conservative structural-margin policy for the canonical request codec.
adr_0023_alternatives: a separately qualified conservative bound over the exact immutable request
accepted_escalation.slice6_constraint: Using the provider input-token-count capability would require an explicit plan/authority amendment and separate owner-controlled external-effect authorization because the accepted Slice 6 sequence forbids it as admission preflight.
blocked_work: M1/S6/WP2 and every later Slice 6 package
all credential, helper-execution, network, and provider work

acceptance_items.title: Price-rule and operation-lifecycle contract shapes
acceptance_items.required: Contracts represent immutable capability/price identity, exact rational nano-USD rules with component-wise upward rounding, finite vectors, authorization, reservation, fence, transport, receipt, overrun, settlement, unresolved hold, cancellation, and replay. WP1 does not implement coordinator reservation/final-gate services, simulator execution, operational settlement, concurrency, or fault recovery.

acceptance_items.title: Answer-free examples and closed-world public authority
acceptance_items.required: Minimal public WP1 examples contain no expected semantic answer, oracle, key, secret, raw bearer transport, or model-derived truth. The exact public package, registry authority, registry schema, resealer, reader, counts, and repository-boundary tests advance together; discovery remains closed-world.

M1 continuation verification profile Layers 1 and 6

authority: Slice 6 plan section 12, Focused verification and Retained evidence
M1 continuation verification profile Common command floor and Layer 6

Retain truthful commands, counts, failures/skips, identities, fingerprints, migration/backup/restore evidence, totality matrix, round trips, forbidden-field scan, input-bound status, traceability, diff, gap inventory, and fresh convergence review. StateTotality is not passing when it exits at the authority stop.

fifteenth_review_closure.finding: Provider-operation JSON future lifecycle was not state-total; reserved could carry downstream terminal identities and projections.
authority: Slice 6 plan section 7 provider-operation schema row
Slice 6 plan section 12 strict round trips and invalid-state totality
fifteenth_review_closure.counterexample: A reserved provider-operation document with receipt, response, usage, or settlement identity/projection passed schema validation.

fifteenth_review_closure.finding: Provider-response JSON used wrong receipt translations and allowed an admitted completed policy overrun.
authority: Slice 6 plan section 7 provider-response schema row
fifteenth_review_closure.counterexample: A completed response whose observed usage exceeded the request limits could remain validation/admission accepted, or receipt vocabulary could disagree between wire and JSON.

fifteenth_review_closure.finding: A known-undispatched cancellation with an existing reservation could not release through settlement.
authority: Slice 6 plan section 12 migration and invalid-state totality
fifteenth_review_closure.counterexample: Cancelled not-dispatched usage correctly omitted transport identities, while a non-hold settlement required them and stranded the exact reservation.

fifteenth_review_closure.finding: Schema-6 post-fact bounds were lower than the domain's doubled absolute bounds.
authority: Slice 6 plan section 8 Price and usage
fifteenth_review_closure.counterexample: Domain-valid retained overruns up to input 147456, output 8192, or 1200000000 nano-USD were rejected by SQL at 73728, 4096, or 600000000.

fifteenth_review_closure.finding: Duplicate terminal credential-intent rows could share one open pending root before event insertion.
authority: Slice 6 plan section 7 schema-6 append-only intent tables and exact invariants
Slice 6 plan section 12 strict invalid-state totality
fifteenth_review_closure.counterexample: Two terminal rows could reference the same pending intent root because root consumption was delayed until a later event.

fifteenth_review_closure.finding: Traceability falsely omitted future authorization, request, reservation, and settlement SQL/protobuf seams.
authority: Slice 6 plan section 12 traceability inventory mapping every field to authority, producer, consumer, persistence, output, and replay
fifteenth_review_closure.counterexample: Representable operation lifecycle fields were marked absent solely because current proof maturity blocks dispatch, despite concrete schema-6 and application-protobuf locations.

fifteenth_review_closure.finding: Future authorization omitted the requested-time deadline bound.
authority: Slice 6 plan section 8 append-only fenced provider-operation transitions
fifteenth_review_closure.counterexample: An authorization with requested_at at or after dispatch_deadline_utc could pass when confirmed_at alone was checked.

fifteenth_review_closure.finding: Helper v1 enum wire values 4 through 7 were reinterpreted, while the gate checked only existence and a self-authored retained value.
authority: Slice 6 plan section 7 helper-private protocol v2 additive identity
fifteenth_review_closure.counterexample: The tracked helper-v1 descriptor assigned new receipt meanings to accepted enum numbers 4 through 7 without a v2-only identity, and the gate did not compare accepted Git bytes.
regressions: eng/verify-m1-slice6.ps1 Contracts accepted-Git helper-v1 identity check

fifteenth_review_closure.finding: Provider-operation lifecycle schema was accumulative rather than discriminated and quantities were unbounded; the application validator accepted reserved plus terminal state.
authority: Slice 6 plan section 7 provider-operation schema row
Slice 6 plan section 8 Provider operation and Price and usage
Slice 6 plan section 12 strict invalid-state totality
fifteenth_review_closure.counterexample: A reserved operation carrying terminal identities/projections and out-of-range quantities passed schema or application validation.

authority: Slice 6 plan section 8 Price and usage
Slice 6 plan section 12 completed domain and wire contracts
fifteenth_review_closure.counterexample: A structurally bounded factual usage receipt above its reservation was discarded instead of retained as overrun and rejected for semantic admission.
